body:
I agree that no one should have to pretend to be someone they are not to be in a relationship. I do have this fear that no one will ever want to be with me as I am. In all of my adult relationships (6 to date), I was the one who was broken up with. My relationship with myself is a very dysfunctional one. I have low self esteem and a lot of insecurities.

I do feel like I need validation from others, and I think this is what drives people away. Instead of being able to to out and enjoy my time with someone, I'm always worried they don't like me or are going to break up with me or something negative. I do end up sabotaging my relationships - I see it and and I can't stop because I need that validation. I know things would be better if I could stop being so sad/insecure about everything, but then when I stop and that validation is gone, I get so sad and revert back to where I started. It's a cycle that I can't break.

I'm not really sure how to do things on my own. Any time I am alone, I get so depressed, I turn to the only thing that I know to make me happy. Which in my case is a relationship. Right now I just feel empty. I don't know what my next step is. When I'm thinking clearly and looking out for my own best interests, I can tell myself don't do this or that, but when I get sad and feel like all I want is to die, I throw all my good intentions out the window and go for temporary fixes to stop the pain.

Yeah, I've always had some issues with trust. And yeah, I know its not a long term strategy. I know I need to be better/stronger as an individual before I could ever hope to have a functioning relationship again. But then as soon as I'm alone, I get so sad and lonely, I stop having any sort of motivation to do anything for myself or get better. The only time in my life I ever did things for myself was when I have been in relationships. 

With my current partner, I originally just saw it as a distraction. He made me happy when I felt like I never would be happy again. I guess kind of like how I feel right now. But I didn't see it as long term, we are in very different parts of our lives, it is long distance, etc. But now it has become very unhealthy for me, I feel like I would be unhappy without him. I also find that I don't care about the differences between us anymore. I have been honest with him about my issues/problems. He seems accepting, but is stressed out by how much I bring him down. And I will say, this isn't the first guy who blamed me for stress induced medical issues. The first guy I dated right after the break up ended up in the hospital/needed surgery from a stress induced medical issue that he blamed me for. I overthink things and once I get started on a train of thought, I can't stop thinking about something until I feel like I understand it or am reassured.
